subject: Dragon Quest II
text: Dragon Quest II is set one hundred years after the events of the first game.

evidence.quote: Dragon Quest II is set one hundred years after the events of the first game.

subject: Dragon Quest II achievement set
text: The achievement set has 0 missable achievements.

evidence.quote: Number of missable achievements|0

subject: Dragon Quest II achievement set
text: Mastering the achievement set takes approximately 15-20 hours.

evidence.quote: Approximate time to master|15-20 hours

subject: Dragon Quest II achievement set
text: The achievement set covers regular progression, character leveling, learned spells, and major collectible items.

evidence.quote: This achievement set covers your regular progression, as well as the leveling of characters and the spells they learn, as well as all the major items that can be collected throughout the game.

subject: Step 1: Progression Achievements
text: Step 1 (progression achievements) totals 218 points.

evidence.quote: [**Step 1: Progression Achievements**](#step-1-progression-achievements--total-points-218)

subject: Step 2: Leveling Achievements
text: Step 2 (leveling achievements) totals 104 points.

evidence.quote: [**Step 2: Leveling Achievements**](#step-2-leveling-achievements--total-points-104)

subject: Step 3: Miscellaneous Achievements
text: Step 3 (miscellaneous achievements) totals 105 points.

evidence.quote: [**Step 3: Miscellaneous Achievements**](#step-3-miscellaneous-achievements--total-points-105)

subject: Spells
text: Spells are learned automatically on level up.

evidence.quote: Spells are automatically learned on level up, so you don't need to go out of your way to learn something.

subject: Step 3: Miscellaneous Achievements
text: None of the Step 3 miscellaneous achievements are missable, and they can be done at any time once enough progress is made.

evidence.quote: None of these are missable and can be done at any time, given that you have made sufficient progress to be able to do them.

subject: Hero
text: Keep progressing until you reach the sea; grinding is only needed when necessary before it.

evidence.quote: Step 1: Keep progressing until you get access to the sea. There isn't much you can do before it besides regular progression, so just grind when necessary and make your way there.

subject: Golden Key
text: Collecting the Golden Key and Jailor's Key is the top priority once you have access to the sea.

evidence.quote: Now that you have access to the sea, collecting the Golden Key and Jailor's Key will be your top priority.

subject: Jailor's Key
text: The Jailor's Key must be bought for 2000G.

evidence.quote: You don't need to do any grinding to get both of these items, although 2000G is needed to buy the Jailor's Key.

subject: Token of Erdrick
text: The Token of Erdrick can be found.

evidence.quote: With access to both keys, you can get a variety of items. You can find the Token of Erdrick (Thou Hast the Crest of Thine Line [achievement 46419]) and exchange it for the Helmet of Erdrick (Thine Ancestral Helmet! [achievement 115785]), the Shield of Erdrick (Thine Ancestral Shield! [achievement 115784]), the Armor of Gaia (Thou Hast the Protection of the Land [achievement 115781]), and the Water Flying Cloth (Thou Hast a Sodden Garment [achievement 115782]).

subject: Water Flying Cloth
text: The Water Flying Cloth can be obtained twice and is recommended as the strongest armour for the Prince of Cannock and the Princess of Moonbrooke.

evidence.quote: Note that you can get the Water Flying Cloth twice, and this is highly recommended as it is the strongest armour in the game for both the Prince of Cannock and that Princess of Moonbrooke.

subject: Water Flying Cloth
text: A second Water Flying Cloth is made by giving the weaver the Magic Loom and Dew's Yarn, then saving and resetting before claiming the dress and handing over the items again.

evidence.quote: To do this, get the Magic Loom and the Dew's Yarn, hand it in to the weaver who will make it into a dress, and then just... get the items again, without saving or shutting the game down. After having collected both items again, save the game and reset, then claim the dress and give him the items again for a second one.

subject: Staff of Thunder
text: The Staff of Thunder is obtained by fighting the clown in the basement of Midenhall Castle.

evidence.quote: To do so, head to Midenhall Castle and fight the clown in the basement to get a Staff of Thunder (Thou Hast the Stick of Sages [achievement 115780]).

subject: Staff of Thunder
text: The Staff of Thunder can be sold for 19,500G, and fighting the clown again after saving and resetting gives another staff.

evidence.quote: You can only have one, but due to a glitch, you can sell this staff for 19,500G, then save and reset, and fight the clown again to get another staff.

subject: Staff of Thunder sell glitch
text: The Staff of Thunder sell glitch can be repeated indefinitely and is a major source of money.

evidence.quote: This can be done infinitely and is an incredible source of money.

subject: Staff of Thunder
object: weapon for the Princess of Moonbrooke
text: After grinding money, obtain another Staff of Thunder to use as a weapon for the Princess of Moonbrooke.

evidence.quote: Make sure that after you are done grinding money to get another one as an actual weapon for the Princess of Moonbrooke.

subject: Falcon Blade
text: Two Falcon Blades cost 25,000G each in Tuhn, for the hero and the Prince of Cannock.

evidence.quote: Two Falcon Blades (25,000G each) in Tuhn for the hero and for the Prince of Cannock.

subject: Sword of Light
text: The Sword of Light costs 16,000G in Wellgarth and is the hero's strongest weapon until the Thunder Sword.

evidence.quote: Sword of Light (16,000G) in Wellgarth for the hero, which will be your strongest weapon until you get the Thunder Sword.

subject: Shield of Strength
text: Shields of Strength cost 21,500G each in Beran, Tuhn, or Wellgarth.

evidence.quote: Four Shields of Strength (21,500G each) in Beran, Tuhn, or Wellgarth.

subject: Shield of Strength
text: The Prince of Cannock equips the Shield of Strength, which works as a free HealMore in battle without needing MP.

evidence.quote: The Prince of Cannock will be equipping this, while all other party members have it in their inventory. In battle it can be used as a free HealMore without needing MP, and is therefore very useful.

subject: Moon Fragment
text: Getting the Moon Fragment opens the path to the Rhone Cave, as an alternative to grinding around Osterfair.

evidence.quote: At this point you can either grind around Osterfair or get the Moon Fragment and open the path to the Rhone Cave.

subject: Rhone Cave
text: Rhone Cave is a tough dungeon best done with careful pathing, fleeing, and the Shield of Strength.

evidence.quote: This is a tough dungeon, but with careful pathing and good usage of fleeing and the Shield of Strengths, you can make it through and also get two additional upgrades for the hero: the Thunder Sword (Thou Hast the Blade of Storms [achievement 115779]) and the Armor of Erdrick (Thine Ancestral Armor! [achievement 115783]).

subject: Thunder Sword
text: The Thunder Sword is one of two hero upgrades received after getting through Rhone Cave.

evidence.quote: This is a tough dungeon, but with careful pathing and good usage of fleeing and the Shield of Strengths, you can make it through and also get two additional upgrades for the hero: the Thunder Sword (Thou Hast the Blade of Storms [achievement 115779]) and the Armor of Erdrick (Thine Ancestral Armor! [achievement 115783]).

subject: Armor of Erdrick
text: The Armor of Erdrick is the second hero upgrade received after getting through Rhone Cave.

evidence.quote: This is a tough dungeon, but with careful pathing and good usage of fleeing and the Shield of Strengths, you can make it through and also get two additional upgrades for the hero: the Thunder Sword (Thou Hast the Blade of Storms [achievement 115779]) and the Armor of Erdrick (Thine Ancestral Armor! [achievement 115783]).

subject: Save point
text: A shrine after Rhone Cave provides a save and respawn point.

evidence.quote: Make it through and head to the shrine to have a save and respawn point.

subject: Giants
text: Giants at the Rhone Plateau drop the Sword of Destruction, with a fairly high drop rate.

evidence.quote: While not necessary, getting the Sword of Destruction as a drop from Giants at the Rhone Plateau is highly recommended, and since the drop rate is pretty high and as you'll be grinding here anyway, chances are you'll get it rather quickly.

subject: Attack power exploit
text: Equipping the Falcon Sword before entering Hargon's Castle, then swapping to the Thunder Sword or Sword of Destruction inside, makes the Falcon Sword hit harder outside.

evidence.quote: Now for the exploit. Head to Hargon's Castle, and before entering the castle, equip the hero with the Falcon Sword. This sword will attack twice, but has lower damage as a result. Now, go inside the castle and quip either the Thunder Sword or the Sword of Destruction. The latter will curse you but don't worry, this is all according to plan. Then go outside the castle, and the Falcon Sword has been re-equipped again, but with the power of either of the swords you equipped.

subject: Equip menu
text: Opening the equip menu recalculates attack power, so it must be avoided when using the exploit.

evidence.quote: Do not open the equip menu as this will recalculate the attack power.

subject: Attack power
text: Attack power recalculates on level up, so stay near the castle when close to leveling.

evidence.quote: When you gain a level, your attack power will also be recalculated, so try to be around the castle every time you are close to gaining a level so you can immediately use the exploit again.

subject: Attack power
text: Dying does not reset attack power, so a low level is not a concern for the exploit.

evidence.quote: Dying will **not** reset the attack power, so don't worry about being too low leveled.

subject: Hero
text: Level 30 is enough for all achievements, though grinding a bit longer helps against the tough bosses ahead.

evidence.quote: Only level 30 is necessary for all achievements, but you may want to grind just a bit longer because the bosses ahead are quite tough.

subject: Attack power exploit
text: The exploit works inside the castle after the Charm of Rubiss is used, including against the bosses.

evidence.quote: However, this exploit **will** work in the castle itself after using the Charm of Rubiss, so you can use this on the bosses as well.

subject: Starting chests
text: One of the two chests downstairs at the start contains the Copper Sword.

evidence.quote: Once you start the game, the king will ask you to follow him downstairs. There are two chests waiting for you, with one of them having the Copper Sword.

subject: Copper Sword
text: Open the menu with the A button and equip the Copper Sword to the Hero.

evidence.quote: Open the menu by pressing the default A button, then equip it to the Hero.

subject: Prince of Cannock
text: From the Castle of Cannock, the king and princess send you to a cave to the east, which then sends you to Midenhall.

evidence.quote: The prince of Cannock and you are unintentionally playing a cat and mouse game. First, head to the Castle of Cannock, which is located to the north-west of the Castle of Midenhall (your starting location). Talk to the king and princess, who will mention the prince is looking for you and went to a cave to the east. Go inside here and make your way to the end, then get told the prince went to Midenhall.

subject: Prince of Cannock
text: The Prince of Cannock waits inside the inn at Leftwyne, south of Cannock and west of Midenhall.

evidence.quote: What the game actually means is that the prince went to the town to the west of Midenhall and south of Cannock, called Leftwyne. The prince of Cannock will be waiting for you here inside the inn.

subject: Silver Key
text: The Silver Key is in Lake Cave, in the far west of Cannock, and the reward waits at the very end of the dungeon.

evidence.quote: The Silver Key is located in the cave to the far west of Cannock called the Lake Cave. Your reward will be waiting for you at the very end of the dungeon.

subject: Lake Cave
text: The quickest route to the Silver Key is the far bottom-left of B1F, then the chest in the bottom-right of B2F.

evidence.quote: The quickest way to get there is to go to the far bottom-left on B1F, then find the chest in the bottom-right of B2F.

subject: Mirror of Ra route
requires: Add the prince of Cannock to the party
text: From Hamlin, going south over the bridge, then south-west to Moonbrooke Castle and straight east, leads to a small marsh where the Mirror of Ra is found.

evidence.quote: First, head to Hamlin which is directly to the south of where you first arrive on the continent. Then, cross the bridge to the south and go south-west to eventually reach Moonbrooke Castle. This castle will give you hints as to where you can find the Mirror, but it is not necessary to obtain it so instead, keep going straight east from the castle. You'll eventually come across a small marsh, and this is where you have to search for the Mirror to find it.

subject: Mirror of Ra
location: small marsh east of Moonbrooke Castle
requires: Add the prince of Cannock to the party
text: The Mirror of Ra is found in a small marsh east of Moonbrooke Castle, on the next continent.

evidence.quote: First, head to Hamlin which is directly to the south of where you first arrive on the continent. Then, cross the bridge to the south and go south-west to eventually reach Moonbrooke Castle. This castle will give you hints as to where you can find the Mirror, but it is not necessary to obtain it so instead, keep going straight east from the castle. You'll eventually come across a small marsh, and this is where you have to search for the Mirror to find it.

subject: Princess of Moonbrooke
text: The Princess of Moonbrooke joins the party after the Mirror of Ra is used on a dog in north-east Hamlin.

evidence.quote: Once you have acquired the Mirror of Ra, head back to Hamlin and find the dog in the north-east corner of town. Use the Mirror of Ra on this dog to reveal the transformed princess, who will then join your party!

subject: Cloak of Wind
text: The Cloak of Wind is in the Tower of Wind, which lies east of Hamlin reached by the northern bridge.

evidence.quote: The Cloak of Wind is found in the Tower of Wind, which is located south of the marsh where you find the mirror, but you need to go east of Hamlin, take the northern bridge there and follow the path to reach it instead.

subject: Tower of Wind
text: On the bottom floor, take the top-right stairs and keep going up; on the floor with two stairs, take the first one to reach the Cloak of Wind.

evidence.quote: On the bottom floor, take the stairs found in the top-right corner, and keep going up until you reach a floor where you can take two stairs. Take the first one, follow the path here, and you'll arrive at the Cloak of Wind.

subject: Dragon Horn route
text: Be sufficiently leveled before the long journey with no rest to the two towers.

evidence.quote: Once you have the Cloak of Wind and have rescued the princess of Moonbrooke, prepare for another long journey with no rest in-between so make sure you are sufficiently leveled.

subject: Cloak of Wind
location: two towers northwest of Moonbrooke Castle
text: Equipping the Cloak of Wind on top of the southern tower and jumping off to the other tower triggers the flight achievement.

evidence.quote: From Moonbrooke Castle, head west, go through the shrine, and head north-west from here until you come across two towers, with you only being able to enter the southern one. Climb to the very top of this tower and stand at the edge. Equip the Cloak of Wind here, and then jump off the tower to land safely at the other tower, triggering this achievement.
